title: What the Satin Bowerbird chooses

is_this_you.pressure: When someone wrecks your work, you rebuild it overnight and say nothing about who did it.
is_this_you.love: You court with a made thing, then wait for them to come back and look twice.
is_this_you.cost: One thing out of place and you stop hearing the compliment about the rest.

opener.text: Darwin called the bower-birds the best evidence that birds have a taste for the beautiful [s13]. He wrote that the satin bower-bird gathers gaily coloured things, blue parrakeet feathers among them, and keeps rearranging them [s13]. In one bower Gould found a neatly worked stone tomahawk and a slip of blue cotton [s13]. You were born a Libra in a Rooster year. Your proof of taste has always been the arrangement.

howto: Three parts, set out in order. Move them around if you like.

tabs.label: Your bower
tabs.intro: Air for the eye. Metal for the finish.

rows.text: Libra is cardinal Air, ruled by Venus, with an eye for fairness and proportion [s1] [s2]. The Rooster is yin Metal, hardworking and very observant, and it keeps its promises [s3] [s4]. Venus picks the pieces. The Rooster polishes them every morning. What you make holds up under close inspection.

The male builds two parallel walls of sticks on the ground, an avenue for courtship and never a nest [s6] [s13]. He chews plant matter with saliva, sometimes charcoal, and paints the inner walls [s6] [s8]. When researchers removed the paint, females came back less often [s11]. You paint the inside wall too. Visitors rarely name it. They feel it.
Young males wear olive-green like the females, and the full blue-black takes about seven years [s6] [s8]. You put in your plain years before anyone saw the colour, and you spent them on the building.

Mature males use more blue than any other colour, though yellow and shiny things and snail shells turn up too [s5] [s6]. That is your rule. A strict palette, with room for the one piece that earns its place. You can tell an exception from a mistake at a glance.

Males raid each other's bowers, wreck them and steal the decorations [s5] [s12]. Each keeps his own bower up all year round [s6]. You guard finished work. You also keep a careful count of what went missing.
Exhibition design and conservation both pay for an eye that spots the one wrong piece.

tabs.label: Who you build for
tabs.intro: Three who look twice. One who keeps correcting your steps.
tabs.love_lead: In love you court with something you made. Most females visit several bowers before they mate with one male [s12], and they come back more than once to look [s11]. You read the second visit as the real yes. The old pairings name three who return.

easy.why: The Secretary Bird (Aries, Dragon year) is your secret friend, since the Dragon is the Rooster's six-harmony partner, and Aries sits opposite Libra [s3] [s1].
The Superb Lyrebird (Gemini, Dragon year) carries the same Dragon bond, and Gemini is Air like you [s3] [s1].
The Vulturine Guineafowl (Aquarius, Ox year) stands in your trine of Ox, Snake and Rooster, and Aquarius is the third Air sign [s3] [s1].

hard.why: The hard one is the Crowned Crane (Libra, Rabbit year): same sign, same taste, but the Rabbit clashes with the Rooster [s3] [s1].

story.text: In Australian slang a bower-bird is a scavenger of trifles, first cited in 1941, and by 1943 a petty thief as well [s14]. The insult misses the point. The real bird keeps only what fits.

closing: Set the last blue feather at the entrance. Whoever sees why it goes there is worth the wait.
